environment: real Store over synthetic in-memory files and backup hashes

checks.name: saving unchanged card content preserves its timestamp, history and persisted data
legacy annotations remain accepted without additive fields
document fingerprints are additive and refresh without changing stable document identity
missing-source recovery candidates require an exact unique content hash match
a unique exact-content return restores the existing document identity and every Store path reference
offline source moves are detected without a delete event and exact-content recovery migrates references
changed-content source stays unresolved until explicit selection, then retains identity and old-version recovery data
a target-sidecar migration conflict preserves both copies, original references, and a recovery record
a failed main-data write rolls back a moved sidecar and retains a migration recovery snapshot
two Store instances serialize disk commits and retain a concurrent edit as a conflict
a failed save keeps the latest edit dirty and an explicit retry persists it
tampered backup bytes are rejected before source or main data changes
a partial backup restore rolls back every file and the live Store when a staged write fails
text/image overlays, deleted state, notebook identity and highlighter brush persist and reopen unchanged
rich text styles survive Store reopen and invalid runs cannot overwrite the sidecar
overlay soft deletion participates in one Store undo/redo while preserving the source annotation/card identity
unsafe or malformed overlay edits are rejected before scheduling a sidecar overwrite
invalid disk overlays block load and preserve the original bytes
a live annotation mutated after scheduling is revalidated immediately before disk write
remote conflict adoption refuses unsafe overlays; choosing the valid local copy remains possible
a hash-valid backup with unsafe overlay data fails staging before any file or main-data mutation
duplicate annotation identities and malformed legacy shapes cannot enter through backups or edits
a handwriting-only canvas counts as study content and survives save/reopen
handwriting patches do not share mutable arrays and whole-stroke changes support undo/redo
erasing the last default-layer stroke removes only the implicit empty container and supports undo/reopen
custom empty sketch layers and legacy empty containers survive save/reopen without load-time migration
an unsupported handwriting version cannot silently erase existing ink
